questions.q: Define the term "इक्यजिकुह" as used in the chapter and state its English equivalent.
questions.a: "इक्यजिकुह" refers to the topsoil layer that is fertile and suitable for cultivation, equivalent to "topsoil" or "arable soil". A wrong answer (e.g., confusing it with "इकरिकुह" or "जस्त.किकुह") reveals that the student has not distinguished the three soil-type terms defined in the text, indicating a gap in technical vocabulary acquisition which is essential for understanding the region's agricultural constraints.

questions.q: Explain in your own words why the author predominantly uses passive voice constructions (e.g., "ओक्यूबज बनाई जाती है", "मिट्टी डाली जाती है") when describing the construction of houses.
questions.a: The passive voice shifts focus from the human agents (masons, labourers) to the process and materials, creating an objective, impersonal tone appropriate for an explanatory/descriptive text about traditional architecture. A wrong answer that merely identifies the passive voice without linking it to the text's informative purpose shows the student can recognize the form but not analyse its functional significance in this register.

questions.q: Given the sentence from the text: "जब ओक्यूबज की दीवारें खड़ी हो जाती हैं, तब छत डालने का काम शुरू होता है।" Identify the clause types (main/subordinate) and the conjunction used, then rewrite the sentence in active voice without changing the meaning.
questions.a: The sentence contains a subordinate adverbial clause of time ("जब ओक्यूबज की दीवारें खड़ी हो जाती हैं") introduced by "जब", and a main clause ("तब छत डालने का काम शुरू होता है"). Active rewrite: "जब ओक्यूबज की दीवारें खड़ी हो जाती हैं, तब मजदूर छत डालने का काम शुरू करते हैं।" A wrong answer that fails to separate the clauses or misidentifies the conjunction indicates weak syntactic analysis skills; an incorrect active rewrite (e.g., keeping "होता है") shows inability to manipulate voice while preserving tense and aspect.

questions.q: Compare the sentence structure and vocabulary density in the paragraph describing soil types (इक्यजिकुह, इकरिकुह, जस्त.किकुह) with the paragraph describing the social life during festivals. What does the difference reveal about the author's stance toward each subject?
questions.a: The soil-type paragraph uses dense nominal compounds, precise technical terms, and declarative sentences with minimal modification, reflecting a scientific, classificatory stance. The festival paragraph employs longer, more complex sentences with descriptive adjectives, cultural vocabulary, and emotive modifiers, reflecting an ethnographic, participatory stance. A wrong answer that only notes "one is technical, the other is simple" misses the nuanced interplay of syntax and lexicon that encodes the author's dual role as documentarian and insider.

questions.q: Critique the author's decision to retain dialect words like "बाखा", "जस्ता", "लद्दाखी" without glosses in the main text. Is this effective for a national-level textbook audience? Justify your position.
questions.a: Retaining dialect words without glosses preserves authenticity and respects the linguistic identity of the region, but it risks alienating readers unfamiliar with Ladakhi terms. Effectiveness depends on the pedagogical goal: if the aim is immersive cultural exposure, it succeeds; if the aim is immediate comprehension, footnotes would be better. A one-sided answer (e.g., "it is good because it's authentic" without acknowledging accessibility issues) reveals an inability to evaluate trade-offs in register and audience design.

questions.q: Write a 4-5 sentence paragraph describing the construction of a traditional house in your own region, deliberately incorporating: (a) at least two passive voice verbs, (b) one technical term (real or coined) for a local material, and (c) a complex sentence with a subordinate clause of reason.
questions.a: A strong response will demonstrate controlled use of passive voice (e.g., "दीवारें खड़ी की जाती हैं", "छत डाली जाती है"), introduce a plausible technical term (e.g., "लाल-मिट्टी-ईंट" or "चूना-पलस्तर"), and embed a reason clause (e.g., "क्योंकि बरसात अधिक होती है, इसलिए ढलवाँ छत बनाई जाती है।"). A poor response that uses only active voice, lacks a technical term, or produces only simple sentences shows the student cannot yet apply the analysed features productively.
